item.title: Milwaukee Brewers aim to complete World Series sweep over Tampa Bay Rays in Game 4
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers look to complete a World Series sweep against the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 4 after winning eight straight postseason games.
item.content:encoded:
I wrote yesterday about how this season was over, and after the drubbing that Milwaukee put on Tampa, it seems almost certain. How certain does it seem? There are people out there saying that the Brewers are cheating. That's how dominant this team has been in the past few games. Tonight marks Game 4 of the World Series, and after getting a win yesterday, let's try to take one more unit this season.

The Milwaukee Brewers are unreal. The team is up 3-0 in the World Series, and they've won eight straight postseason games. Overall, the team is 10-1 in the postseason, and the lone loss was by just one run. If you want to find any "flaw" for the team, it might be that they are only winning by one run in about half of the games. That doesn't leave much room for error, but when your team doesn't have any errors, it really doesn't matter. The Brewers broke out the bats yesterday and left nothing to chance last night.

The Brewers have not announced a starter for tonight's game, which means they are likely to go with some sort of opener or a bullpen game. I would assume they will start Dustin May, but it's possible they go a different direction. Maybe they will send out Jacob Misiorowski. He threw in Game 1 on Friday, so it would be a bit of a short rest. Either way, the team is set to potentially win their first World Series title ever. If they don't go with a starter today, their bullpen has covered more than half of the innings in the postseason, and they have an ERA under 1.50 for the playoffs.

BREWERS RALLY PAST CHAOTIC LATE-GAME REPLAY, PREMATURE CELEBRATIONS TO WIN FIRST WORLD SERIES GAME IN 44 YEARS

The Tampa Bay Rays are done. Is it this game? Maybe, but maybe not. Either way, the team is done. They aren't going to beat the Brewers four games in a row. At this point, their winning one or two games would seem like a miracle. They gave up eight runs in the fifth inning last night, and it just felt like one of those times when the Rays had to be praying for any sort of stop to end the inning. By the time it was over, the Rays were down 10-0. They scored a meaningless run late in the game.

In an effort to keep their season alive, the team is turning to Griffin Jax. It feels like they may be waving the white flag, but there really isn't a better option for Tampa in this one. In the regular season, Jax went 8-10 with a 3.53 ERA and a 1.18 WHIP. The numbers were both solid, and he is a big reason the Rays are here for the season. However, in the postseason, he has thrown six innings and allowed four earned runs. This is his first appearance in 12 days.

RAYS' CHANDLER SIMPSON CRASHES FACE FIRST INTO WALL WHILE MAKING INCREDIBLE CATCH IN WORLD SERIES VS BREWERS

Jax faced the Brewers earlier this season when he was working out of the bullpen. He was fine in his first appearance, going one inning and allowing no runners. In the second game, though, he was rocked. He allowed five runs, three earned, on three hits and one walk, without recording an out. I'm not really sure what the Rays can do differently to keep this season alive. Give me Milwaukee to win and finish the sweep tonight.

item.title: WNBA's bizarre national anthem controversy shows just how much the league needs Caitlin Clark
item.description: Caitlin Clark's absence from the WNBA Finals exposed how the national anthem controversy went unnoticed all season for the Dream and Valkyries.
item.content:encoded:
Caitlin Clark isn't quite the women's basketball equivalent of Tiger Woods, but there's a reason she's been compared to the 15-time major champion.

She brought millions of new eyeballs to a league that had long struggled for mainstream attention. She's also a marketing juggernaut, with endorsement deals from the likes of Nike, Gatorade and State Farm. But like Tiger in his prime, perhaps the greatest measure of Clark's star power is that when she's absent — the audience is, too.

Nothing illustrates that phenomenon better than the WNBA's national anthem controversy.

WNBA SILENT AFTER FINALS TEAMS SKIP NATIONAL ANTHEM DESPITE RULE REQUIRING PLAYERS TO STAND AND LINE UP

All year long, players and coaches from the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries have been running off the court before the Star-Spangled Banner is played. Then, just after "the home of the brave" is sung, they return to the floor. Neither team has publicly explained why it follows this routine, nor have they said what the players and coaches do during those 90-some-odd seconds. But the wildest part of all this is that, until these WNBA Finals — nobody seemed to notice.

If an NFL or NBA team had engaged in a similar practice during the regular season, it would be one of the biggest sports stories — or even news stories — in the country. Pundits would be regularly weighing in on the matter, activists would be mobilizing, and a nationwide debate on the issue would ensue.

WNBA FINALS: ANGEL REESE HEADLINES CHAMPIONSHIP SHOWDOWN AS LEAGUE SEEKS TO DRAW VIEWERS WITHOUT CAITLIN CLARK

But until now, it had barely even generated a whisper. Do you think that would be the case if the Fever left the court for the anthem?

The answer, of course, is "absolutely not." The actions of Clark and her teammates would be dissected every day. POTUS would probably comment, and some of those endorsement deals would be in jeopardy. But a Caitlin-free WNBA game simply doesn't matter to the majority of American sports fans. The scheduled start time for Game 6 speaks to that.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Monday, it was announced that what could be the final WNBA game of the season will be played at 12:30 p.m. Eastern time on a Thursday. The reasoning is that the Dream wanted a venue change — moving the game from Gateway Center Arena (capacity 3,500) to State Farm Arena (17,000). The problem is that the Hawks are scheduled to play that same day, meaning Game 6 will occur when most Americans are working or in school. Again, it's hard to believe that happens if Clark and the Fever were involved.

This national anthem mystery is one of the more bizarre sports stories I've ever seen. That players and coaches have repeatedly left the court without offering an explanation is strange enough. That it's taken this long for anyone to notice might be even stranger.

But this is what happens when the league's true needle-mover isn't on the court. Caitlin Clark has made the WNBA impossible to ignore. Without her, apparently, it's still remarkably easy.

item.title: Israelis vote in record numbers in first national election since the Oct. 7 Hamas massacre
item.description: Israel election exit polls show Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud and Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar locked in a fight with neither bloc reaching 61 Knesset seats.
item.content:encoded:
TEL AVIV, Israel — Israelis turned out in exceptionally high numbers Tuesday for the country’s first national election since the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas massacre, with initial exit polls showing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud emerging as the largest party but his governing coalition falling short of a parliamentary majority, potentially opening the door to a change in leadership.

The projections released by Israel’s three major television networks after polls closed at 10 p.m. local time (4 p.m. ET) showed Likud winning 25 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, compared with 23 seats for former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party in Channels 12 and 13 exit polls, and 21 seats according to Kan 11.

The projected parliamentary balance showed 50 seats for Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc, 53 for the main opposition parties and 17 for Arab parties, leaving neither major bloc with the 61 seats generally needed to form a government.

Although Netanyahu’s party is projected to remain the largest in parliament, his political future is far from secure. The opposition parties, together with the Arab factions, would hold a combined 70 seats, although that does not mean they would necessarily agree to form a government together.

FORMER ISRAELI ARMY CHIEF GADI EISENKOT EMERGES AS NETANYAHU’S LEADING ELECTION CHALLENGER

The results set the stage for potentially weeks of coalition negotiations, with the possibility that Netanyahu could lose power despite Likud finishing first.

The results are preliminary projections, not an official vote count, and could change as ballots are tallied in the coming days.

The election followed an extraordinary day at polling stations across Israel, with long lines and voter participation reaching levels not seen in decades.

Israeli voter turnout surged to a historic high, with 55.7% of eligible voters casting their ballots by 4 p.m. local time (10 a.m. ET), according to Israel's Central Elections Committee. The figure marked the highest turnout recorded at that hour since measurements began in 1973, underscoring the intensity of the country's national election.

The unusually high participation prompted election officials to streamline voting procedures and assure voters that anyone arriving at a polling station before the 10 p.m. deadline would be allowed to cast a ballot.

The vote was widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu's leadership following three years of war and continuing questions about responsibility for the security failures that allowed Hamas terrorists to kill approximately 1,200 people and abduct 251 others on Oct. 7, 2023.

JD VANCE DECLINES TO ENDORSE NETANYAHU DESPITE TRUMP'S STRONG BACKING

Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, campaigned on his record of confronting Iran and its regional proxies, highlighting Israel's military achievements and his relationship with President Donald Trump.His opponents accused him of failing to accept responsibility for the October 7 security failures and opposed his government's approach to investigating the failures that preceded the massacre.

Throughout the final hours of the campaign, Netanyahu, Eisenkot, former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett and other party leaders mounted an intensive effort to mobilize supporters and win over undecided voters.

Netanyahu's Likud party prepared hundreds of targeted campaign videos and social media messages, making digital outreach a central part of its last-minute election strategy.

Eisenkot's campaign pushed supporters to rally behind Yashar as the leading alternative to Likud, while Bennett traveled between cities and engaged voters directly and through WhatsApp conversations.

NETANYAHU FIGHTS FOR POLITICAL FUTURE AS ISRAEL HEADS TO POLLS WITH IRAN THREAT LOOMING

The campaign's closing hours also featured personal appeals, phone calls to undecided voters and aggressive turnout operations across the political spectrum.

The final days were particularly important because a relatively small share of voters remained undecided about which party to support.

A Times of Israel poll published five days before the election found that 87% of respondents had already made their final choice, while 2.4% remained undecided between the pro- and anti-Netanyahu political blocs.

Other surveys suggested a larger pool of undecided voters, although many were choosing between parties within the same political camp rather than switching sides.

That distinction could prove decisive in Israel's parliamentary system, where political parties need at least 3.25% of valid votes to enter the 120-seat Knesset.

Even a slight change in the vote share of smaller parties could shift several parliamentary seats and determine whether either camp has a realistic path to power.

TRUMP SAYS NETANYAHU NEEDS TO BE RE-ELECTED, OR ELSE US WILL HAVE TO 'FINISH THE JOB’ AGAINST IRAN ALONE

Despite the exit poll projections, the identity of Israel's next prime minister may remain uncertain for weeks.

Unlike in the United States, Israelis vote for political parties rather than directly electing their head of government.

The 120 seats in parliament are allocated proportionally, and parties must secure at least 3.25% of valid votes to win representation.

Once the final results are certified, Israeli President Isaac Herzog will consult with the newly elected political factions and select the lawmaker he believes has the strongest chance of forming a government.

That candidate will have 28 days to negotiate a governing coalition, with the possibility of a 14-day extension.

Official results are scheduled to be published by Nov. 4. Until a new government takes office, Netanyahu's outgoing government will remain in power.

item.title: Cruise vacation comes to crashing halt as ship slams into 2 cargo vessels
item.description: The Mein Schiff 3 collision in Bremerhaven, Germany, damaged lifeboats and forced TUI Cruises to cancel the entire Canary Islands cruise for shipyard repairs.
item.content:encoded:
A luxury cruise ship slammed into two cargo vessels during stormy weather in Germany and abruptly brought a planned trip to the Canary Islands to an end.

The incident took place in Bremerhaven, Germany, Sunday as the Mein Schiff 3 was departing the port.

TUI Cruises confirmed the incident to Fox News Digital and said no passengers were injured.

ANGRY CRUISE PASSENGERS SAY FRUSTRATING ISSUE SHOULD HAVE BEEN DISCLOSED BEFORE BOOKING

"As a result, we have decided to cancel the planned cruise to the Canary Islands," the spokesperson said. "We very much regret having to take this step."

Technical teams and experts inspected the ship shortly after the collision.

They determined it would need repairs at a shipyard, a TUI Cruises official told Fox News Digital.

The collision was reported by Bremen Police on Sunday evening. Officials said the cruise ship collided with two container ships during stormy weather before returning to Columbus Quay.

OUTRAGED CRUISE PASSENGERS SOUND OFF ABOUT 'IMMENSE DISAPPOINTMENT' AFTER ABRUPT CANCELLATION

"According to current knowledge, no one was injured in the collision," the translated police statement said.

"Information on the exact extent of the damage and the cause of the accident is not yet conclusively available."

Footage posted to Reddit appears to show a view from the cruise ship during the collision, with at least one person shouting as the vessel scrapes against a cargo ship, damaging lifeboats along its side.

Bremen police said they're investigating the collision. Police also reportedly opened an administrative offense investigation into the captain of the Mein Schiff 3, according to German broadcaster NDR.

THOUSANDS BOOKED TROPICAL BAHAMAS CRUISE AND ENDED UP IN FREEZING CANADA INSTEAD

The TUI Cruises spokesperson said the safety of passengers and crew remains the company's "top priority."

"We believe this is the only responsible decision and the right course of action to maintain our high safety standards," the spokesperson said.

"Our focus now is on keeping our guests fully informed, supporting them and assisting them with the next steps."

The incident and video prompted discussion online, with users expressing sympathy for affected passengers.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"Imagine saving for years, saving up your holidays just to go on a cruise and then this happens when deploying to the sea," one Reddit user said.

"Ooof. That looked expensive," another chimed in.

One Reddit commenter claimed to have been aboard another cruise ship in Bremerhaven that was scheduled to depart shortly after the Mein Schiff 3.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"I'm actually on a different cruise ship in Bremerhaven that was supposed to leave shortly after Mein Schiff 3 last night," the user wrote. "Shortly before we were supposed to leave, they announced the port was closed. It was really windy."

The commenter said his or her ship had originally been scheduled to stop in Hamburg but was diverted because of the weather.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"I can't see the damage but Mein Schiff 3 is docked back in port," the Reddit user added. "I can see it from the bridge cam."

Other cruise vacations have faced similar disruptions in recent months.

Passengers aboard a Royal Caribbean cruise ship were left scrambling earlier this year after their seven-night Alaska voyage was abruptly canceled due to technical problems.

Earlier this spring, a small cruise ship struck a reef near the Fijian island where Tom Hanks' movie "Cast Away" was filmed.

item.title: Internal emails reveal Colorado school official predicted trans volleyball fallout before public letter
item.description: Dakota Ridge High School emails reveal district leaders planned weeks ahead for the transgender volleyball controversy but left coaches without guidance.
item.content:encoded:
"I heard that meetings were held weeks ago to discuss a plan for this scenario, which is unfolding exactly the way it was predicted."

Dakota Ridge High School Athletic Director Jeff Legault sent that warning in an urgent Oct. 6 email to district leadership, contradicting the official account from Jefferson County Public Schools, Colorado's second-largest school district.

In internal emails provided to OutKick, Legault was addressing the fallout after a transgender athlete secured a spot on the girls' junior varsity volleyball team while dozens of female students were cut.

Behind closed doors, district officials sought to keep the controversy quiet, advising staff to give brief replies, point uncomfortable female athletes to separate changing spaces and cite student privacy laws to avoid addressing the dispute publicly.

TRANSGENDER ATHLETES HAVE TAKEN 2,293 CHAMPIONSHIP SPOTS FROM BIOLOGICAL WOMEN, NEW RESEARCH FINDS

In an official letter to parents, the district later described the situation as an "unfamiliar circumstance." Yet internal records show administrators had met weeks earlier to plan for the controversy, predicting both the locker room privacy concerns and the parent outrage over cut players.

When those issues surfaced, central district leadership delayed. Dakota Ridge coaches and building staff were left fielding angry calls with no approved script, caught between two separate battles over lost spots on the court and privacy in the locker room.

During fall tryouts at Dakota Ridge, coaches had cut upwards of 35 girls from the program, including juniors who had earned spots during their freshman and sophomore seasons. Concerned parents pushed back, arguing the school had compromised legal protections designed to preserve athletic opportunities for girls.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Once the season started, concerns quickly shifted to privacy inside the girls' locker room.

The first documented warning arrived on Friday, October 2, when a parent emailed Legault and head coach Matthew Zeman to report that players were discussing the situation among themselves.

In the message, the parent wrote that several families felt their daughters' privacy rights were being pushed aside to protect the confidentiality of the transgender player.

Legault forwarded the complaint up the chain of command, warning district officials that this email was just the beginning. District leadership initially tried to keep responses brief. District Compliance Officer Emily Sloan advised Legault to offer a short, polite reply thanking the parent for their perspective. 

If the parent had a child on the team, she suggested adding a single sentence stating that all students can request accommodations in the locker room. The district's communications director agreed with this approach, opting to handle broader concerns about fairness by treating them as individual requests for private changing spaces.

That approach fell apart within days. By the morning of Tuesday, Oct. 6, Legault sent an urgent email to the district's executive team pointing out the gap between the district's internal planning and its execution. Legault reminded them that leadership had met weeks prior to prepare for this outcome, yet the coaching staff had never received the promised talking points.

Inside the building, Legault described a chaotic environment. Office assistants and teachers were dealing with angry parents, while the volleyball coaching staff tried to prepare for league playoffs while fielding complex questions about federal equality laws from teenagers.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Furthermore, the district's chosen talking point, offering separate locker room accommodations to uncomfortable girls was failing.

When staff offered these alternative spaces, players and parents responded by questioning the overall equity of the situation. The fallout soon reached beyond volleyball. Legault reported that some student-athletes were questioning whether to continue playing sports at all, with several already deciding against trying out for the upcoming women's basketball season.

Frustrated by the delays, Legault asked for a written response for the volleyball community that same day. He warned that waiting for an afternoon meeting was inadequate because players would be using the locker rooms for a game that very night. He pointed out that the school administration and coaching staff were "taking the blame" while the district remained silent.

This internal pressure prompted Jeffco leadership to act. The communications department circulated a draft statement for legal and administrative review, and on Oct. 7, the district sent an official letter to Dakota Ridge volleyball families.

The finalized statement built directly on the emails from earlier that week. The district made no mention of roster cuts or missed athletic opportunities for female players. Instead, officials pointed to state anti-discrimination policies intended to ensure all students have "equal access to educational programs, facilities, and district-sanctioned activities" regardless of gender identity or expression. 

They formalized the plan discussed on Oct. 2, asking female athletes to request alternative changing spaces if they wanted more privacy, and cited federal privacy rules to avoid discussing the specific student involved. Finally, the letter asked families to avoid public speculation and social media discussions.

National attention followed after parents took their concerns to the media. A formal complaint alleged that high school players faced benching threats from their coach if they discussed the transgender athlete among themselves.

An email screenshot obtained by OutKick showed Zeman informing a parent that a player would miss an upcoming match over reported bullying. In the email, Zeman wrote that the program emphasizes "character, respect and how players treat one another," describing the student's reported remarks as "falling short of its standards."

Parents alleged that the players were only permitted back on the court on the condition that they agree not to discuss the issue again. "We have seen emails showing that girls were threatened to be benched because they were expressing their frustration in a very adolescent manner," Lindsay Datko, founder of the advocacy group Jeffco Kids First, previously told OutKick's Jackson Thompson.

Neither Jeffco Public Schools nor Dakota Ridge High School responded to OutKick's requests for comment.

That local controversy is now intertwined with a broader legal battle. Federal civil rights regulators previously found that Jeffco Public Schools violated federal equality laws through its athletic policies. The district is currently suing the federal government, arguing that federal demands conflict with Colorado state law.

The dispute at Dakota Ridge precedes a statewide vote on Proposition 134. The ballot initiative would require all public school athletic programs to designate rosters and facilities based on biological sex, establishing a uniform state law to replace district-by-district policies.

item.title: Chicago cardinal sparks controversy by honoring abortion-access donor at gala for future priests
item.description: Chicago Cardinal Blase Cupich faces growing backlash for plans to honor Michael Sacks, whose family foundation gave $500,000 to Planned Parenthood.
item.content:encoded:
A prominent Catholic cardinal is facing backlash over plans to honor a wealthy Democratic donor who gave hundreds of thousands of dollars to organizations supporting abortion access at a fundraising gala benefiting the education of future priests.

Chicago Cardinal Blase Cupich is scheduled to recognize billionaire Michael Sacks at the Oct. 29 Rerum Novarum Awards Dinner benefiting Mundelein Seminary, according to the event's announcement.

Between 2020 and 2022, the Sacks Family Foundation, of which Sacks is president and treasurer, reportedly contributed grants totaling $500,000 to Planned Parenthood of Illinois, raising questions about the recognition in light of the Catholic Church's longstanding opposition to abortion.

According to a report from Crain’s Chicago Business on Sept. 29, Sacks and his wife, Cari, gave $600,000 to the Prairie State Access Fund, an initiative established in partnership with the administration of Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker to support abortion access in the state. Sacks is a board member of the Obama Foundation.

EXCLUSIVE: PLANNED PARENTHOOD SET FOR MASSIVE TAXPAYER WINDFALL IF SENATE FAILS TO ACT

The planned honor comes roughly a year after Cupich faced criticism from fellow Catholic leaders over plans to recognize Sen. Dick Durbin, D-Ill., whose support for abortion rights drew objections from bishops who argued that honoring him would conflict with Church teaching. Durbin declined to accept the lifetime achievement award following the backlash. 

In a Monday statement defending the recognition for Sacks, Cupich wrote in part, "This year, the Nostra Aetate Award will be added to the honoring ceremony. It is named for the Declaration on the Relation of the Church to Non-Christian Religions, issued by the Second Vatican Council, and is designed to affirm the value the Church places on interreligious relationships by honoring members of non-Christian communities for their leadership in their own and the wider community. This year’s recipient is Mr. Michael Sacks, a well-respected leader in Chicago and in the Jewish community."

Cupich further defended the decision, arguing that the Catholic Church's Nostra Aetate declaration provides a framework for honoring and building relationships with individuals who do not share Catholic beliefs, including those who hold differing moral or political views. He maintained that recognizing someone for their leadership and service to the community does not constitute an endorsement of all their positions, but instead fosters mutual respect and creates opportunities for meaningful dialogue.

‘BARBARIC’ ABORTION PROVISION FUELS CHRISTIAN PUSH TO CRACK DOWN ON DEM GOVERNOR

Carl E. Olson, editor of the Catholic World Report, called out Cupich on X Monday, writing, "A pro-abortion billionaire is being given a prominent award by the @archchicago because he's ‘well-respected’ in Chicago and the Jewish community. In defending the choice, @CardinalBCupich plays the antisemitic card, saying, ‘Refusing to honor or engage with Jews solely because they hold conflicting religious or political positions can risk mimicking historic patterns of antisemitism through exclusion and bigotry, which, frighteningly, is on the rise.’"

POPE LEO PROMOTES ARCHBISHOP WHO BARRED PELOSI FROM COMMUNION TO ONE OF VATICAN'S HIGHEST COURTS

Olson added, "Surely there are prominent pro-life Jewish leaders in the Chicago area? Also, what if, theoretically, it were discovered that Mr. Sacks had given money to a pro-MAGA group? Would the antisemitic card still be used?"

Catholic investigative reporter Christine Niles also took to X to raise concerns, sharing a quote from the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops' statement "Catholics in Political Life," which reads, "The Catholic community and Catholic institutions should not honor those who act in defiance of our fundamental moral principles. They should not be given awards, honors or platforms which would suggest support for their actions."

In a statement to Fox News Digital, Kelsey Reinhardt, president and CEO of CatholicVote, said, "The U.S. bishops have taught that Catholic institutions should not give ‘awards, honors or platforms’ to those who act in defiance of our fundamental moral principles. A little over a year ago, Catholics made clear their disappointment that the Archdiocese of Chicago attempted to honor a public supporter of abortion."

Reinhardt added, "We urge Cardinal Cupich to reconsider this honor. The pre-born babies and the faithful who support them cry out once again."

The media relations department for Cupich told Fox News Digital that it has nothing to add to the statement on its website.

In a statement to Fox News Digital, a spokesperson for Sacks said, "Mr. Sacks is honored to receive the award and believes the Cardinal's statement speaks for itself."

Fox News Digital reached out to the USCCB for comment.

item.title: Utah grovels to Pat McAfee, WNBA’s brunch game is peak stupid & why you should take your dogs on vacation
item.description: Campaign text messages, Pat McAfee's war with Utah, and the WNBA's absurd 12:30 p.m. Finals tip-off all highlight this edition of "Nightcaps."
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com.

One week until Election Day.

Now, don't you go clicking away on me. You did not accidentally stumble upon a column about politics and who you should vote for and what's at stake, blah blah blah.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

No, I'm just here to gripe about something that seems to be a new phenomenon this midterm season: campaign text messages.

Look, I know that if you sign up for a candidate's text messages, you will get inundated with a steady stream of pleads for donations.

But I would never sign up for something like that. So tell me why I get a dozen text messages a day from various state and local politicians — attacking their opponents, begging for my vote, detailing BS stories about how they grew up in a middle-class family where "nothing came easy" and they learned the "real value of a hard day's work."

Delete. Report spam. Every time.

Look, voting is important, and we should all do it. I'm glad to live in a country where we actually get a say in who's making our laws and affecting our quality of life.

But unsolicited campaign text messages should be illegal.

Not to mention they just feel like bad practice. How do you think bombarding me with an endless string of text messages will somehow endear you to me? It actually makes me not want to vote for you.

Is everyone dealing with this right now? Is this a new thing or have I somehow just managed to avoid the onslaught until this campaign season?

November 3 truly can't come soon enough. Next Tuesday, we party.

But until then, let's do some Nightcaps.

Wow oh wow, College GameDay was AWKWARD on Saturday.

It all started with that girl who was chosen for the kicking contest. Now, admittedly, I love the kicking contest. Every Saturday, I yell to my husband, 'It's time for the kick!' and we run into the living room to watch.

This Saturday, I knew it was doomed from the start. As soon as I saw the contestant.

Now, don't get me wrong. I'm all about girl power. I am, after all, a girl. And I have no doubt there are plenty of women who can kick a 33-yarder. Soccer players obviously come to mind.

But the last couple of times they've had women competing, they've been women with the athleticism of a potato.

This isn't an anti-woman thing. Obviously. Plenty of men have missed, too. But if you — either gender — know you have an absolutely 0% chance of nailing this kick, why even put your name in the raffle? Why embarrass yourself like that?

And to make matters worse, she had the gall to tell Pat McAfee he should be giving her $3 million to make the kick — not the $1 million she was already offered.

Girl.

My skin is crawling with awkwardness.

Anyway, we found out yesterday there was a lot more under the surface about GameDay’s trip to Utah that we didn’t see.

Before the show, Utah’s official social media account posted a video of students doing impressions of Pat, including one calling him "corny" and another saying his shirtless bit was "creepy." Pat said he had no problem with random students roasting him, but he did have a problem with the university itself amplifying it right before he was about to go on national TV and promote their school.

He said the whole thing made him feel "very, very uncomfortable," especially given the very real safety threats he and other public figures face, and even referenced the Charlie Kirk assassination while explaining why it bothered him. By the end of GameDay, Pat picked Houston to beat Utah and told the crowd, "I’ll never see you again, hopefully."

Utah has since apologized, saying the post was meant to be lighthearted but "missed the mark," and that Pat and the GameDay crew are always welcome back.

Something tells me Pat will not be taking them up on that invitation anytime soon.

But what do we think, guys? Was Pat being dramatic? Or is Utah insufferable? Or both?

While we're on the topic of insufferable, though ...

There’s an old saying that goes something like: "A lack of preparation on your part does not constitute an emergency on mine."

Someone should print that out and tape it to the front door of WNBA headquarters.

Because Game 6 of the WNBA Finals — a game in which the Golden State Valkyries could literally WIN THE CHAMPIONSHIP — will tip off Thursday at 12:30 p.m. ET.

That is 9:30 IN THE MORNING for Golden State fans. Hope nobody scheduled a Zoom meeting.

Here’s how we got here: The Atlanta Dream normally play at the 3,500-seat Gateway Center, but they wanted their Finals games at the much larger State Farm Arena, home of the Atlanta Hawks. The problem is State Farm already had conflicts on every single Atlanta Finals date, including a Hawks-Cavaliers game Thursday night.

The league managed to shuffle Games 3 and 4 around those conflicts, but somehow got all the way to a guaranteed Game 6 before figuring out what the hell to do with this one.

And listen, I understand wanting the bigger arena. But I also understand planning ahead, which apparently no one bothered to do.

The Hawks were always scheduled to play Thursday. This did not sneak up on anybody.

Yet now EVERYONE has to move heaven and earth because the Dream doesn’t want to play the biggest game of its season in its actual home arena.

FROM ANTHEMS TO DEFINITIONS, THE WNBA KEEPS DOING DUMB THINGS, AND THE REASON FOR IT WILL LEAVE YOU SPEECHLESS

The Hawks pushed their game back an hour. State Farm Arena employees have to flip the building between games. Broadcast partners have to rearrange programming. Staff, security, vendors, parking attendants and fans all have to adjust.

And the Valkyries’ fan base gets to watch a potential championship celebration on their office laptops while pretending to answer emails at 9:30 a.m. Pacific.

Warriors coach Steve Kerr was asked about the situation and joked that it was better than playing at the YMCA in front of 75 people.

item.title: Museums hide mummies from public view due to lack of 'consent' from ancient Egyptians or their descendants
item.description: Glasgow museums removed ancient Egyptian mummies from display over consent concerns, citing a revised code of ethics on human remains dignity.
item.content:encoded:
Two museums in Scotland have reportedly removed ancient Egyptian mummies from public view out of concern that they were displayed without the consent of the deceased.

Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum is one of several museums in Glasgow, Scotland, that have changed their policies on displaying human remains. The BBC reported that Glasgow Life, which manages Kelvingrove, removed the mummified remains of the Egyptian priest Nekht, who lived more than 3,500 years ago, along with his painted coffin, in the "absence of consent from the deceased individual or their descendants."

A spokesperson for Glasgow Life told Fox News Digital, "The removal of human remains from display at Glasgow Life museums reflects contemporary museum practice."

"The International Council of Museums’ revised Code of Ethics, published in June 2026, states that ‘Museums should uphold the inherent dignity of human remains and promote respect for their significance,’" the spokesperson continued. "The All-Party Parliamentary Group on Afrikan Reparations 2025 report, ‘Laying Ancestors to Rest,’ also raises ethical concerns about the display of ancient Egyptian human remains due to the consistent disregard of the potential wishes of the ancestors and the intention of the communities that originally laid them to rest."

LIBERAL ARTS COLLEGE DROPS PROF’S NAME FROM CAMPUS HALL AFTER GRAVE DIG CONTROVERSY

"Glasgow Life Museums’ draft Human Remains Policy proposes that human remains should only be displayed where there is documented and informed consent from the deceased individual or, in appropriate circumstances, their descendants," the spokesperson concluded. "In the absence of such consent, we believe removing ancient Egyptian human remains from display is more respectful to the deceased individuals."

The Hunterian, another museum in Glasgow, said the elaborate sarcophagus, or decorated coffin, of Lady Shep-En-Hor will remain on display, but her mummified remains will be covered going forward.

When contacted by Fox News Digital, the Hunterian provided a press release which said, "As part of its commitment to becoming a more ethical institution, The Hunterian at the University of Glasgow is considering its holdings of archaeological and anatomical human remains across all sections of its collections."

Museums have faced growing questions about the ownership and display of artifacts acquired from other countries, particularly during periods of Western colonial rule. The Hunterian's decision also raises questions about whether museums should treat human remains from the United Kingdom differently from those originating abroad.

LOUVRE TURNS AWAY TOURISTS AS PARIS BRACES FOR RENEWED VIOLENCE FOLLOWING DESTRUCTIVE RIOTS

"Human remains are among those items which The Hunterian seeks most keenly to return to their communities and nations of origin," the statement continued. "The Hunterian is also re-assessing what will be on display to the general public and, as part of its duty for the respectful care of these collections, it has decided to no longer put human remains from outside the UK on open display."

"After in-depth consideration and consultation with experts, including Egyptologists, The Hunterian has decided to continue to display Lady Shep-En-Hor’s sarcophagus as a fine work of Late Period Ancient Egyptian funerary art, but to cover the mummified person, so she can no longer be viewed," the statement added, specifying that "The Hunterian takes the view that the Lady Shep-En-Hor deserves privacy in death."

The decisions follow a revision to the International Council of Museums' (ICOM) Code of Ethics, which calls on museums to "uphold the inherent dignity of human remains and promote respect for their significance," according to the BBC report.

"Decisions about these items and collections should be made in collaboration with descendants or communities from which they originate, if known," the ICOM guidance added. 

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Steph Scholten, a professor who serves on ICOM's ethics committee, told the BBC that the guidelines can be interpreted differently by institutions.

"What the code of ethics puts forward is that these topics need careful consideration and decision making, they do not suggest one fixed outcome. Kelvingrove and The Hunterian have come to slightly different outcomes about our displays," he said. "The code of ethics does not prescribe that all human remains should be taken of display."

item.title: Cheerios makes major change to cereal boxes after years of consumer complaints
item.description: Ninety percent of cereal eaters take extra steps to keep cereal fresh. Cheerios and Ziploc finally answered with their resealable PantrySeal cereal bag.
item.content:encoded:
Cheerios is giving its familiar cereal box an upgrade that could put an end to rolled-up bags, cereal clips and stale O's.

The General Mills brand has teamed up with Ziploc to introduce Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal, a resealable bag inside a traditional cereal box.

The new packaging is designed to open only partially across the top, creating a pour spout that can then be resealed to help keep cereal fresh.

YOUR FAVORITE GROCERY AND SNACK ITEMS MAY HAVE DISAPPEARED FROM STORE SHELVES IN 2026

The change comes after years of consumers asking for an easier way to close cereal bags, according to General Mills.

The company said Cheerios and Ziploc receive hundreds of thousands of requests, comments and reactions annually about cereal packaging.

A December 2025 survey conducted by consumer insights platform Suzy revealed that 90% of cereal eaters take additional steps to preserve freshness after opening a box, including using clips, clothespins and cereal containers.

"Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal takes a small, everyday cereal frustration and finally gives consumers the simple solution they've been asking for," Emilie Knox, vice president and business unit director for Cheerios at General Mills, said in a statement.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

It's a frustration cereal fans have also aired on social media.

"Why don't cereal companies use Ziploc type bags?" one Reddit user asked in a 2024 post that received hundreds of upvotes.

Other users have questioned why resealable packaging has not become standard for cereal.

"They could of did this 30 years ago. People have been asking for ages," one Reddit user wrote earlier this year.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"Cheerios just solved one of the biggest childhood problems," another person wrote on X after learning the news.

The new PantrySeal differs from a traditional Ziploc bag. Its zipper-style closure stops partway across the top of the bag, leaving an opening designed to make pouring easier and reduce spills.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The packaging will initially be offered as an option for original Cheerios and Honey Nut Cheerios rather than replacing the traditional bags in all boxes.

Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal became available exclusively through Walmart beginning Oct. 27 and is expected to roll out to retailers nationwide in the coming months.

item.title: ‘Kate & Allie’ star Susan Saint James dead at 80

item.content:encoded:
Susan Saint James, the actress known for "McMillan & Wife" and "Kate & Allie," has died.

Saint James, 80, died Monday after a battle with pancreatic cancer, People magazine reported.

"She never met a stranger. Every person she met became the most important person in the room at that moment, from a fellow board member to the clerk at the shoe store, who usually walked away knowing her entire life story," a representative told People.

"Her defining act: weeks after losing her youngest son, Teddy, in the November 28, 2004 plane crash, she delivered his eulogy as a note to each of her other children and her husband, giving them words to heal. Even in the deepest grief of her life, she put everyone else first. Days after the crash she sat with Tim Russert to thank the people who had reached out and to tell them the family was okay."

HOLLYWOOD STARS WHO DIED IN 2026

"She brought that same fire and positivity to everything that followed, and never lost it," the statement continued.

Saint James began her career modeling before switching gears to television. Her breakthrough came in 1968 when she landed the role of research assistant Peggy Maxwell on NBC's "The Name of the Game." Her performance earned her a Primetime Emmy Award in 1969 and established her as one of television's rising stars.

She earned her biggest fame as Sally McMillan, the plucky wife of Rock Hudson’s San Francisco police commissioner Stewart McMillan, in the hit series "McMillan & Wife" from 1971-1976.

She is also known for roles in "Love at First Bite," "How to Beat the High Cost of Living," "M*A*S*H," "Law & Order: SVU" and "Suits."

She was previously married to Richard Neubert and makeup artist Tom Lucas.

After "Kate & Allie" ended, Saint James largely stepped away from Hollywood to concentrate on her family and charitable work, particularly her longtime involvement with the Special Olympics.

item.title: Sen Flávio Bolsonaro reportedly flees Brazil for US after election loss
item.description: The Brazilian far-right senator has reportedly headed to Florida two days after losing the presidential runoff to leftist incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
item.content:encoded:
Brazilian Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro has reportedly left Brazil for the United States on Tuesday, two days after losing the country's presidential runoff to leftist incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

An ally of the far-right conservative senator confirmed his departure to Reuters on Tuesday.

Bolsonaro's flight is reportedly headed to Florida, according to Brazilian outlet Metropoles, citing people close to his family.

The 45-year-old lawmaker had been out of public view since Tuesday morning, the outlet reported.

BRAZIL’S RAPID ELECTION COUNT PUTS SPOTLIGHT ON VOTING SECURITY AHEAD OF US MIDTERMS

His reported departure came as a deadline for him to surrender his regular and diplomatic passports expired at noon Tuesday. Brazilian newspaper Folha de São Paulo reported Bolsonaro was under investigation for alleged money laundering and other crimes. 

It remained unclear whether Bolsonaro had complied with the order, The Associated Press reported.

Bolsonaro was served with the order Monday, one day after Lula defeated him in Sunday's presidential runoff.

BRAZIL BECOMES NEXT TEST FOR LATIN AMERICA’S SURGING CONSERVATIVE MOVEMENT

With 100% of the vote counted, Lula won 51.8% of the vote, defeating Bolsonaro by nearly 4.4 million votes.

He has refused to concede the election and has called for the election results to be annulled, alleging fraud, according to The Associated Press.

Lula addressed supporters after winning re-election to a fourth, nonconsecutive term, expressing gratitude to the Brazilian people.

CONSERVATIVE WAVE HITS ROADBLOCK IN BRAZIL AS LULA HOLDS OFF BOLSONARO CHALLENGE

"No one is required to like the president-elect, but he must govern for everyone," Lula said.

Referring to his opponent, Lula said, "This was a defeat for denialism and lies."

item.title: 175 Democrats demand Trump admin stop Ilhan Omar investigation, warn it could hurt her re-election bid
item.description: Rep. Pramila Jayapal led 175 House Democrats in accusing DHS and DOJ of weaponizing the federal investigation into Ilhan Omar's immigration history.
item.content:encoded:
Nearly 200 House Democrats are moving to shield Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., from further investigation after federal investigators raided her Washington, D.C., home earlier this month.

Rep. Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash., led 175 members of the House Democratic Caucus in a letter to Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin and Attorney General Todd Blanche, criticizing the probe into Omar's immigration history as a partisan attack and accusing them of trying to sway her bid for another term in Congress.

"Congresswoman Omar is seeking reelection in Minnesota’s 5th congressional district in just one week. News of the search warrant, whether properly predicated or not, could affect voters’ decisions, which is exactly why federal law enforcement should not engage in such conduct when voters are casting their ballots. This type of interference strips Minnesotans of their right to a free and fair election guaranteed to them under the Constitution," the letter said.

"We stand with Congresswoman Omar and condemn the weaponization of law enforcement against her. You have already disgraced the offices you hold, and we demand you refrain from taking any further actions that could affect the outcome of the upcoming election."

DEMOCRATS' FURY OVER ILHAN OMAR RAID DRAWS STINGING GOP REMINDER ABOUT RAID FROM THE PAST: ‘SET THE PRECEDENT’

Omar, D-Minn., is under federal investigation over allegations she or her father lied about her birth year on immigration paperwork to obtain her citizenship when her family fled Somalia in the late 1990s. If she was 17 when her father obtained citizenship, as previously thought, she would have automatically qualified along with him. If she was 18 or older, which federal officials now suspect, she would have had to make her own application.

FEDERAL AGENTS RAID ILHAN OMAR’S DC HOME AMID IMMIGRATION FRAUD INVESTIGATION

Her fellow House Democrats recounted the allegations in their letter, saying, "Your probe into the congresswoman reportedly concerns her late father’s filing of immigration paperwork after she fled Somalia’s civil war at age eight, making her a U.S. citizen at age seventeen."

But they argued it does not justify "a pre-dawn raid on her home for paperwork her father filed when she was a minor."

DEMOCRATS HAVE ‘DIRTY HANDS’ OVER COMPLAINTS ABOUT OMAR RAID WEEKS BEFORE ELECTION, EX-PROSECUTOR SAYS

Federal agents executed a judicially authorized search warrant on Omar's home on Oct. 12, seizing multiple phones and notebooks, among other items.

"This weaponization of law enforcement to harass a sitting Member of Congress 22 days before an election is unprecedented and unacceptable," Democrats' letter said. 

"DOJ has long followed a policy not to take investigative steps relating to a candidate this close to an election if delaying the action will not jeopardize a criminal investigation, a policy which Attorney General Blanche has previously invoked as far back as nine months before an election."

ILHAN OMAR BELIEVES TRUMP RAID ON HOME WAS MEANT TO 'INTIMIDATE AND SCARE PEOPLE' FROM VOTING

They argued the probe was "driven by a pre-determined political outcome rather than an objective pursuit of justice."

Omar has dismissed the probe as a political hit job against one of Trump's loudest critics.

Others, however, like House Majority Whip Tom Emmer, R-Minn., have called for Omar to be jailed and deported if the accusations are proven true.

Fox News Digital reached out to DHS and the Department of Justice for comment.

item.title: Former NWSL player says league culture pressured athletes to support political messages they opposed
item.description: Elizabeth Eddy says NWSL players faced pressure to wear political shirts or risk teammate backlash, describing a culture with no room for dissent.
item.content:encoded:
After spectators displaying a "Save Women’s Sports" banner were confronted by other fans and removed from Friday’s Portland Thorns game, former NWSL player Elizabeth Eddy is calling out a league culture she says pressures players to support political messages they do not necessarily believe.

Eddy, who retired earlier this year after an 11-year professional career, told OutKick that the confrontation left her "really, really disheartened" but "not surprised at all." Her concerns extend beyond the stands to team environments where, she says, supporting a cause could become a test of being a good teammate.

"Hey, everyone wear the shirt, be a good teammate, be a good ally," she recalled.

But behind those public displays, Eddy said, "there was like no room to voice a different opinion."

For the retired NWSL veteran, that message created a difficult choice: publicly support a position she did not share, cover it with a sweatshirt or explain herself to people she depended on to succeed on the field.

OLYMPIC LEGEND KAILLIE HUMPHRIES OPENS UP ON IMPACT OF WOMEN'S SPORTS ADVOCACY ON TEAM USA RELATIONSHIPS

"There was a lot of times where that was like the situation where you either wear it, you wear a sweatshirt over it, or you just flat out say, ‘I’m not wearing this,’" Eddy said.

"And then the repercussions of saying you’re not going to wear it on different teams in different political or social causes have different, I would say, responses and none of them are great."

Eddy, who announced her retirement in March after an 11-year professional career, is describing what she considers a gap between the NWSL’s public messaging and the private beliefs of some players. Her account centers on social pressure, team relationships and the perceived cost of disagreeing, rather than a specific disciplinary action she says was imposed for refusing a shirt.

She said the expectation to present a united front could leave little space to question a cause.

"There was like no room to voice a different opinion," she said.

Eddy described players being directed toward reading material when they disagreed. "Reeducate yourself" was how she characterized that response.

Her criticism comes from someone who spent years moving through the league’s locker rooms. Eddy played for the Western New York Flash, North Carolina Courage, Sky Blue/Gotham, Houston Dash and, most recently, Angel City FC. Her Angel City tenure ran from 2023 through 2025.

One example she cited was Angel City’s "Immigrant City Football Club" campaign. The club introduced the shirts in June 2025 as a show of support for Los Angeles’ immigrant communities, describing the campaign as a reflection of the city and the people within the organization.

Eddy said she was not dressing for the game, she recalled and watched from the stands, so she did not have to wear that shirt.

But she said players preparing to compete could feel that questioning a message was another distraction from the job they were trying to do.

"Most girls, I don’t really think believe in a lot of the stuff that they’re getting told to wear, and then like publicly parade around like they’re supporters of it," she said.

Asked specifically about messaging supporting transgender people, Eddy recalled teammates wearing shirts she believed said "protect trans kids." She acknowledged uncertainty about whether wearing them was required.

"I don’t remember if it was ever mandated or not," she said.

She said she did not think she personally had to wear the shirt because she may have been injured or not selected for that weekend. Asked what she would have done if she had been playing, she described a possible workaround.

"So I’d probably wear a sweatshirt over it and not deal with it," she said.

Eddy also pointed to Megan Rapinoe as a major influence on the political culture she described within the NWSL.

Asked how much Rapinoe helped shape that environment, Eddy answered, "significantly, a lot."

But Eddy also expressed respect for Rapinoe’s willingness to speak her mind, recalling that her outspoken positions initially challenged prevailing views.

"I mean, she's been a very outspoken person, her whole career," Eddy said. "I respect a person who's going to speak their mind."

Over time, Eddy argued, that influence helped move the broader group toward Rapinoe’s positions while others remained quiet.

"And then eventually that speaking over and over again, the group starts just going that way in the sense of like no one else is speaking," she said.

Eddy suggested that Rapinoe’s success afforded her a level of freedom to express opinions that less established players might not feel they have. Her criticism centered on what she viewed as an imbalance in whose opinions could be expressed comfortably.

The league’s collective bargaining agreement contains a protection relevant to political messaging. In its article governing promotional and other appearances, it prohibits the league and teams from compelling participation in an appearance requiring support for messaging that conflicts with a player’s sincerely held political, moral, philosophical or religious beliefs. How that provision applied to the warmup situations Eddy described would require additional details about the events and instructions involved.

Eddy herself participated in the union’s work: The NWSL Players Association lists her on the bargaining committee for the agreement reached in 2024. That deal guaranteed contracts, expanded free agency and prohibited trades without player consent.

Her concern, she said, is that an athlete can have reasons to remain quiet even when a disagreement does not result in formal punishment.

In a team sport, she argued, preserving relationships becomes part of protecting a career. Players have to train, compete and depend on one another while navigating disagreements that extend beyond soccer.

"But you almost like slowly keep compromising your beliefs the longer you’re in the system," she said.

Eddy publicly challenged the league’s approach to sex eligibility in an October 2025 New York Post opinion piece calling for clear standards for the women’s category. The article prompted public criticism from her teammates and a statement distancing Angel City from her views.

The club said it respected an individual’s right to express an opinion while maintaining its commitment to "equity, inclusion, and belonging."

Angel City captain Sarah Gorden and goalkeeper Angelina Anderson also addressed the article publicly. Gorden said teammates were hurt by it and objected to its language.

"We don’t agree with the things written for a plethora of reasons, but mostly the undertones come across as transphobic and racist," Gorden said at the time.

Eddy said she subsequently heard through teammates that some players agreed the league should have eligibility rules, even if they disagreed with how her position had been presented.

She believes an active player taking a similar position could face professional consequences, although she acknowledged she could not specify what those would be.

"I think there would be like significant consequences. I don’t know what those would be," she said.

She said a player’s experience would depend on the general manager, coach and city. Her prediction does not establish that a player has been disciplined for expressing those views.

The NWSL has said policy changes would involve its player's association. Commissioner Jessica Berman said in August that every player competing in the league had been determined eligible and that changes to written policy or practice would be made in consultation with the union.

Eddy’s latest comments followed the Oct. 23 confrontation at Portland’s Providence Park, where supporters of female-only sports displayed XX-XY Athletics shirts and a "Save Women’s Sports" banner before a filmed confrontation and security removals. The Justice Department and City of Portland have separately confirmed reviews of the incident.

"I was really, really disheartened," Eddy said when asked about what happened.

She encouraged people who share her position to make their views known and consider where they spend their money. Asked whether she would attend a game and join the demonstrators, she stopped short of making a commitment.

"I will consider that," she said.

Eddy also said disagreement should lead to conversation rather than exclusion.

"It’s uncomfortable and it’s hard and it’s messy, but I think it’s the right thing to do," she said.

For her, the issue has become inseparable from a career she spent years trying to preserve.

"I love sports. I love soccer," she said. "And to have an 11-year career playing professionally and then to come to realize like, wow, this thing I’ve given a lot of my life to really turned in on itself."

The NWSL told OutKick, "The NWSL does not comment on statements by former players," in response to Eddy's comments.

item.title: Is that campaign merch store official? Here's how to tell
item.description: Attaxion researchers found 30 fake Texas campaign merchandise stores traced to just two sellers hawking gear for competing Republicans and Democrats.
item.content:encoded:
You're scrolling online when you spot a campaign T-shirt supporting your favorite candidate. The website looks professional, the merchandise looks legitimate and the address includes the candidate's name. You might even see the word "official" at the top of the page. So, you assume your purchase supports the campaign. But what if the candidate has nothing to do with that store?

With the Nov. 3 midterm elections approaching, new research shared with CyberGuy reveals a troubling discovery in Texas. Researchers at cybersecurity company Attaxion identified 626 unofficial election-related domains, including 30 online merchandise stores presenting themselves as official campaign shops.

Attaxion says it could not verify an official campaign connection for any of the 30 stores. Even more surprising, researchers found that nearly all appeared to come from just two sellers offering merchandise for competing Republicans and Democrats. The findings arrive as the FBI warns about election-related scams involving fake merchandise, fraudulent donations and websites designed to steal personal information. And while this investigation focuses on Texas, the warning signs apply to elections and online shopping across the country.

Join our upcoming CyberGuy LIVE class: 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money

In this free live online class, Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will share five practical ways to protect your trip and your wallet this holiday travel season. You’ll learn how to secure your phone and personal information, find better travel deals, avoid common scams, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Join us Saturday, October 31, at 11 AM ET / 8 AM PT. Register free now at CyberGuyLive.com.

DON'T LET FAKE ELECTION WEBSITES FOOL YOU BEFORE 2026 MIDTERMS

Texas voters are already heading to the polls. Early voting for the Nov. 3 general election began Oct. 19 and continues through Oct. 30. Meanwhile, researchers are finding that candidates' names have become valuable online real estate. Attaxion, a cybersecurity company that helps organizations identify vulnerable websites and other online threats, examined domains connected to the state's U.S. Senate race, governor's race and six competitive congressional districts. The investigation also included websites resembling election offices and voter information pages.

Researchers initially identified 704 domains. After excluding 25 official sites and another 53 domains connected to campaigns or election offices, 626 unofficial addresses remained. Of those, 553 had DNS records when checked. That means the domains had some internet configuration, although it does not establish that each hosted an active website. The Senate race accounted for 323 unofficial domains. Another 75 referenced House candidates, while 70 used gubernatorial candidates' names. The remaining domains referenced election offices or general election-related terms.

Importantly, an unofficial domain is not automatically a scam. Some may belong to supporters, critics or independent businesses. Others may be registered without hosting an active website. However, the researchers identified a smaller group that deserves closer attention.

Of the 626 unofficial domains, Attaxion identified 30 online stores that presented themselves as official merchandise sellers for Texas political candidates. The stores promoted products associated with Republican U.S. Senate candidate Ken Paxton and Democratic opponent James Talarico. Others used the names of Republican Gov. Greg Abbott and his Democratic challenger, Gina Hinojosa.

Researchers also identified stores featuring congressional candidates. Alexandre François, research contributor at Attaxion, worked on the investigation and shared the findings with CyberGuy. "Two things stood out. The first is how little the politics seem to matter to the people selling," François told CyberGuy.

He explained that nearly all the stores appeared to come from the same two sellers, despite promoting candidates from opposing parties. In Texas' 23rd Congressional District, researchers found stores supporting the Republican and Democratic nominees that appeared to share an operator. That raises an obvious question. If a business is selling merchandise for competing candidates, is it really connected to either campaign? According to the investigation, none of the 30 stores could be verified as campaign-operated.

Attaxion traced most of the merchandise websites to two seller identities: ShirtGoat and madetoprints. ShirtGoat appeared to operate 12 stores and was likely connected to two more. Meanwhile, madetoprints was associated with another 15. The researchers found that both sellers used similar website templates while swapping out candidates' names and merchandise. Some sites also borrowed slogans that appeared on official campaign products.

For example, when Talarico's campaign responded to a political nickname with an "I'm a Talafreako" shirt, similar products appeared in three unofficial stores. "It suggests that the motive is most likely commercial rather than political," François explained. "Someone with a political agenda would be unlikely to sell merchandise for both sides of the same race."

Researchers also noticed that several domains were registered on the same day. Some stores reused identical policies with only the candidate's name changed. A few terms-of-service pages even contained apparent chatbot responses left behind during the creation process. That suggests some operators may be creating these stores quickly and repeatedly. However, the researchers could not establish the legal identities of the people controlling all the websites.

One of the biggest challenges is how convincing the stores can appear. A website might feature professional product photos and familiar campaign slogans. It may also offer a functional shopping cart with a normal-looking checkout. Those features can create confidence before someone even thinks to check who operates the business. François says that assumption can be risky. "The first thing to know is that appearance is no longer a reliable guide. With AI, anyone can quickly build a polished store with well-written text, so the old signs of poor design and clumsy language rarely apply, and neither does the word ‘official.’"

Attaxion found that none of the 30 unofficial stores included the campaign-related "Paid for by" disclosure the researchers expected to see. However, independent businesses selling political merchandise are not automatically required to display campaign finance disclaimers. The missing disclosure is one warning sign, not proof of fraud or a legal violation. The stores also failed to provide a verifiable company identity and business address. Some listed a seller name or customer service email address. However, those details did not establish an official relationship with a candidate.

To investigate the websites, Attaxion compared them against verified campaign information from the Federal Election Commission and Texas Ethics Commission. Researchers also examined registration records and revisited the stores on Oct. 20 to check their contact pages, policies and checkout processes. None of those checks established a connection to the campaigns.

119,000 FAKE SHOPS COULD STEAL YOUR CREDIT CARD DETAILS

The researchers uncovered another unusual example involving an expired election website. The domain elpasoelections.com sounds like it could belong to an election office in El Paso, Texas. However, it previously served El Paso County in Colorado. That county used the address for election information for years before allowing its registration to lapse in February 2026. A domain buyer acquired the address in May.

When researchers examined the website, it displayed an online casino promoting itself to Australian users. The investigation identified a new registrant organization associated with Hong Kong, although that record does not independently establish who operates the casino.

François highlighted the discovery as an example of how a once-legitimate web address can change hands. "It is a good reminder that a familiar-looking address does not tell you who holds it today."

The example extends well beyond politics. An expired website previously used by a government office, nonprofit or business can eventually lead somewhere completely unrelated. For accurate Texas election information, the state's official website is VoteTexas.gov. For voting information elsewhere in the country, you can start with Vote.gov.

The Texas findings follow an Oct. 15 warning from the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center. The agency warned that criminals exploit political campaigns to target people across the United States. Some scammers impersonate candidates to solicit fraudulent contributions. Others advertise political merchandise that customers never receive.

The FBI also warned about fraudulent voter-registration messages that direct people to websites designed to collect personal information. Artificial intelligence can make these schemes harder to recognize. Criminals can generate convincing written messages and realistic voices that appear to come from legitimate organizations. However, there's an important limitation to the Texas investigation.

"At this stage we do not know. We did not place test orders, and our research does not include payment records or customer complaints, so we have no evidence either way," François told CyberGuy.

The researchers also did not investigate whether the operators promoted their stores through Google ads, social media or political text messages. They did examine observed DNS traffic and found that some unofficial domains had received lookups. However, those records cannot establish how someone discovered a website or whether they completed a purchase. The findings raise concerns about misleading campaign connections without proving that all the stores committed fraud.

These precautions apply to political merchandise stores and fundraising pages nationwide. They can also help you recognize ordinary shopping scams and websites that impersonate trusted organizations.

Before buying political merchandise or making a donation, find the candidate's established campaign website. Look for the merchandise or contribution page linked directly from that website. For federal candidates, you can also use the Federal Election Commission's database to verify campaign committees and find their reported information. If you're shopping from an unfamiliar retailer, visit its official website independently rather than following a promotional link. This approach also works when someone claims to represent a bank, charity or government agency.

Scammers and unauthorized sellers can register web addresses that closely resemble legitimate ones. Look for misspellings or added words that make an unfamiliar address appear trustworthy. Don't assume a website belongs to an organization simply because the address contains its name or the word "official." You can also use a WHOIS lookup to investigate when a domain was registered. A newly created website deserves closer attention, especially when it claims to represent an established organization. However, domain age alone cannot establish whether a website is legitimate. And remember, HTTPS encryption protects information while it travels between your browser and a website. It does not prove that the site's operator is trustworthy.

WHY VERIFIED SOCIAL MEDIA ACCOUNTS CAN STILL LEAD YOU INTO A SCAM

Before contributing to a political campaign, confirm the organization receiving the payment. Federal political committee websites generally must include a disclaimer identifying who paid for the communication. When applicable, the disclosure also identifies the campaign or committee that authorized it. Look for a "Paid for by" statement and compare the information with official campaign records. Many political campaigns use fundraising platforms such as ActBlue or WinRed. Others use different payment systems. The key is reaching the contribution page through the campaign's verified website. Independent businesses may legally sell political merchandise without supporting a campaign. However, they should not mislead you about who receives your money. A missing or suspicious disclosure deserves attention, but a disclaimer alone does not guarantee legitimacy.

Take a closer look at any online store you've never used before. Search for the company name along with terms such as "reviews," "complaints" or "scam." Read its return and refund policies. Look for a legitimate way to reach customer support. The Better Business Bureau at bbb.org/ can be another place to check for complaints, although the absence of complaints does not prove a company is trustworthy. If you cannot establish who operates a website, consider buying elsewhere.

A scammer may send a message claiming that your voter registration needs attention. Another might pressure you to contribute immediately or purchase merchandise before an offer disappears. The same tactics appear in fake bank alerts and fraudulent delivery notifications. Avoid clicking payment or account-verification links in unsolicited messages. Instead, open the organization's established website yourself. For election-related messages, check information through Vote.gov or your state election office. Be especially cautious about messages asking for passwords, Social Security numbers or payment details.

When shopping online, paying with a credit card generally gives you stronger protections if an order never arrives or a charge is incorrect. Avoid unfamiliar sellers that insist on payment through gift cards, cryptocurrency or wire transfers. Those methods can make recovering your money difficult. Keep your purchase confirmation and review your statements after paying. Also, check whether a political contribution involves recurring payments before submitting it. The FTC's online shopping guide explains how to research sellers and protect yourself when making purchases.

A suspicious shopping site may ask you to create an account before checking out. Never reuse a password from your email, banking or other important accounts. Use a password manager to create unique passwords and enable two-factor authentication (2FA) when available. Strong antivirus software can also help detect malicious downloads and block some dangerous websites. However, it cannot verify whether a political merchandise store is actually affiliated with a campaign. Be selective about the information you share, especially when you cannot verify who operates the website. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com.

If you've purchased merchandise or sent money through a questionable website, act promptly when something appears wrong.

If you entered sensitive identity information into a suspicious website, visit IdentityTheft.gov for personalized recovery guidance.

What stands out to me about this investigation is that the people behind these stores appear willing to sell merchandise for candidates on both sides of the same race. That raises serious questions about what shoppers are being led to believe. I have no problem with an independent business selling political merchandise. But I do have a problem when a website gives people the impression they're supporting an official campaign without making clear who's actually taking their money. And here's something else worth remembering. The FBI is already warning about election scams involving merchandise that never arrives and fake donation requests. Meanwhile, AI makes it easier than ever to create a convincing website. I wouldn't judge a store by its design or the word "official" in its address. I'd go straight to the organization I want to support and use the links it provides. The same advice applies when you're shopping online or responding to an unexpected request for money. A few extra moments of checking can make a difference.

Have you ever purchased something from a website you thought was official, only to discover later that it wasn't connected to the company or organization you wanted to support? Should websites that falsely claim official affiliations face tougher consequences? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

item.title: Shouting match erupts at UN as Cuban foreign minister moves toward US ambassador's podium: 'Back up!'
item.description: United Nations Ambassador Mike Waltz told Cuba's foreign minister to "back up" after he approached the podium as Waltz was making his address.
item.content:encoded:
U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz told Cuba's foreign minister to "back up" Tuesday after the Cuban diplomat approached the podium and interrupted his remarks on the floor of the U.N. General Assembly.

"Well, we know. We know where it went. And today we are here to share it to the world," Waltz said as he accused Cuba's government of enriching its leaders while its people suffered.

As the Cuban delegation sought to interrupt his remarks, Waltz fired back.

"I know you don't like to hear this," Waltz said. "This is America, my friend. This is the United Nations. This isn't your communist dictatorship. You cannot silence me."

CUBAN EXILE-TURNED-CONGRESSMAN UNLOADS ON DEM SENATE HOPEFUL OVER CUBA REMARKS

Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla continued toward the podium as the president of the General Assembly attempted to restore order, reminding delegates that they would have an opportunity to respond.

"This individual needs to back away from this podium," Waltz said as the confrontation escalated. "He's not going to intimidate me in the United States of America.

"I'm the representative of the United States of America. Back up! Back up, Ambassador. Back away! This isn't Havana."

CUBA’S ECONOMIC FREEFALL IS HIDING A NATIONAL SECURITY THREAT JUST MILES FROM FLORIDA: REPORT

The confrontation erupted during the General Assembly's annual debate over the decades-old U.S. embargo on Cuba, with Waltz urging member states to reject a resolution calling for an end to the restrictions.

Waltz accused Havana's communist government of enriching itself while blaming Washington for hardships he said were caused by corruption and repression inside Cuba.

After Cuba was eventually granted the floor, the delegation's foreign minister accused Waltz of "lying" and asked the General Assembly president to call him to order.

"Mr. Waltz is lying yet again," he said, arguing that the U.S. ambassador's remarks were "beneath the dignity of this forum and member states" and were insulting to Cuba's government and people.
